key_insight: A symmetric graded-mesh FEM with L1 time stepping and an auxiliary-variable reformulation yields a stable and convergent solver for time-fractional diffusion-wave equations with constant delay.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical discretization framework for delayed anomalous-diffusion and wave-like processes where standard time stepping can lose accuracy or stability.
method: Reformulate the delayed fractional PDE as an equivalent coupled system using a symmetric fractional-order reduction and auxiliary variable w.
Discretize time with the L1 scheme on a symmetric graded mesh and space with standard finite elements.
Prove stability via a discrete fractional Grönwall inequality and derive local error estimates using a new barrier-function comparison principle.
evidence_signal: The paper reports theoretical stability and error estimates, and states that numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence behavior.
watch_item: The method depends on symmetric graded time meshes and a carefully constructed barrier-function analysis, so implementation is more specialized than standard uniform-mesh FEM.
paper_title: Galerkin finite element method for time fractional diffusion-wave equations with constant time delay
